findings.assessment: Lifecycle exists on host session options; only a publisher is installed in a fresh tool context. Missing or failed begin clears inherited publishers. API/native send/stream and sequential/parallel paths forward the lifecycle. Server begin captures identity before tool code and allocates an execution UUID independently of provider call ID.

findings.area: Actual protected outcome and receipt preservation
findings.assessment: Protected execution retains existing schema, principal, approval and beforeToolCall checks. Complete receives its actual envelope before distillation and foundation requires outer success plus canonical non-failed data. Begin, complete and diagnostic callback rejection do not substitute a publication error for the tool result or add producer replay. Known mutating tools remain single-attempt under existing protected retry policy.

findings.area: Lazy capture and all-output failure boundary
findings.assessment: Byte/path/ordinal capture occurs synchronously inside the low-level failure boundary; size and output count are checked before allocation. Malformed first input reports a failure without lazy initialization. Rejected later staging aborts the publication signal, preventing a prior subset commit. Pending stages are awaited even when producer code omitted its own await; complete closes the set and is idempotent. Late stages reject without reopening.

findings.disposition: no blocker found within stated limits
findings.assessment: Abort releases lazy-root initialization wait and a late resolver checks cancellation before entering the service. Detached initialization rejection is observed. Real filesystem/DB I/O is not universally interruptible, and host diagnostic callbacks are not durable publication-failure receipts.

Returned artifacts JSON is not read for publication authority. Current authorization and actual admitted roots remain mandatory host configuration. Legacy artifacts still pass to existing consumers; no strict delivery cutover, main AgentService activation, owned-chat fencing or restart guarantee is established.

limitations: Independent work consisted of source review, exact-byte/hash checks and read-only patch applicability. Owner tests were inspected, not independently rerun; owner 70 tests/331 assertions is not an additional independent passing suite.

Owner bounded union includes 20 new tests across two new files and 50 existing regressions; no full production TypeScript, live provider/native SDK, real browser/channel or OS confinement test is proved here.

Only the two shared core seam files are present in this owner source; component.patch applies its seven owned paths atop the separately frozen complete producer source. This is patch compatibility evidence, not combined runtime activation or combined regression evidence.

Production authorizer/root inventory, main/task/subagent/playground wiring, selected-existing-file capture, durable session listing and HTTP/channel/share/history/UI consumer migration remain required before strict artifact attribution claims.
Existing legacy artifacts, including forged copied metadata, still reach legacy consumers unchanged. Absence of new DB publication authority does not make those consumers safe.
Current role/revocation checks retain foundation non-atomic callback windows. Run/session IDs do not constitute versioned execution ownership or durable lease fencing.
Generic trusted lifecycle hooks can block if their own promises never settle; concrete lazy initialization has abort handling, but this is not universal I/O timeout or cancellation proof.

Publication diagnostics are separate, non-blocking observers rather than an atomic durable failure log. Distillation may still fail after successful publication; future delivery must query durable publication authority rather than depend solely on copied history metadata.
No Atlas/Hermes parity, superiority, provider-independent quality, complete artifact race fix, or restart/power-loss claim follows from this isolated component.
